rationale: C01 provides the strongest concrete template. Both veto messages reject a private-claim bill while expressly proposing a narrower substitute that would send the claimant through established adjudicative procedures: first determine the underlying legal entitlement or status, then allow recovery only under generally applicable law. This alternative-bill mechanism is more distinctive and material than the broader uniform-treatment reasoning shared with C03 and C18. C03 and C18 are nonetheless strong secondary parallels because they reject individualized legislative exceptions that bypass general benefit rules.

shared_material.child_excerpt: I would, therefore, be willing to approve a bill which would permit a determination of the claimant's employment status at the time of his injuries and which would then permit him, notwithstanding any statute of limitations, to file a claim under the law applicable to that status.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: While I would not object to a measure which would merely permit Sedgwick County to secure a judicial determination in the Court of Claims of the question as to whether the tax assessed against the property involved was lawful, without creating any new cause of action
shared_material.explanation: Both conclude by specifying an acceptable substitute bill that permits adjudication of an existing legal claim without legislatively creating or dictating a special award.

shared_material.child_excerpt: In this way the claim will be processed under accepted procedures, fair to both the individual and the Government.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: without creating any new cause of action
shared_material.explanation: The shared administrative principle is to preserve ordinary claim-processing machinery rather than grant exceptional substantive relief.

shared_material.child_excerpt: Its sole justification seems to be that the claimant is unable to meet the substantive and procedural requirements of compensation statutes of general applicability.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: Moreover, such provisions would discriminate against all other claimants.
shared_material.explanation: Both characterize special private relief as an unjustified departure from rules applicable to other claimants.
